title: Methods for predicting the fire behaviour of fibre reinforced thermoset composites
authors: Pomázi, Á.; Magyar, G.; Toldy, A.
institution: Budapest University of Technology and Economics (BME)
venue: Polymer Degradation and Stability 245:111857 (DOI - resolved via Crossref bibliographic search; open-access PDF at pt.bme.hu)
reported_value: FULL dataset (train+test combined): XGBoost 0.96 (best). HELD-OUT test+validation only: RFR 0.30 (best of the three algorithms; XGBoost 0.25, ANN 0.13)
eval_set_size: 75 samples total (15 input params); + 4 additional experimentally-prepared validation composites (0/1/2/3 wt% P via RDP flame retardant, tested via MLC)
split_method: Random split for the 75-sample database (paper states 'random split method'); PLUS a separate small externally-measured validation set (4 samples) added on top of the random test split.
notes: Full text obtained (open-access PDF hosted at pt.bme.hu, BME's own repository). IMPORTANT: the paper's own abstract/conclusion headline claim of R2=0.96 (XGBoost, pHRR) and R2=0.95 (RFR, TTI) is Table 8's FULL-DATASET fit (includes training data, i.e., not a true held-out metric). Table 9 - the actual held-out 'test and validation datasets together' - shows drastically weaker generalization: pHRR R2 best=0.30 (RFR), TTI R2 best=0.58 (ANN, not RFR as the abstract implies for full-dataset), THR R2 best=0.67 (XGBoost), CR R2 best=0.82 (RFR). This is a critical fairness issue: if Dravix is compared against this paper's headline numbers, that comparison is apples-to-oranges (in-sample fit vs true generalization) - Dravix's held-out numbers should be compared against Table 9, not the abstract's R2=0.96/0.95. Given the tiny dataset (75 samples, only 4 true external validation samples) this is actually one of the WEAKEST real held-out benchmarks found in this survey and should be relatively easy to beat on true generalization. Source: full text at http://www.pt.bme.hu/publikaciok/2012_open_2025%20PDST%20Methods%20for%20predicting%20the%20fire%20behaviour%20of%20fibre%20reinforced%20thermoset%20composites.pdf
